name: Zellige Cobalt
story: Cobalt glazes are used across Moroccan ceramic tilework.

name: Zellige Verdigris
story: Green and blue-green glazes are common in zellige palettes.

name: Zellige Jade
story: A glazed green drawn from the color range of hand-cut tiles.

name: Zellige Ink
story: Deep blue tile accents read almost black in shaded interiors.

name: Zellige Turquoise
story: Turquoise glazes bring a clear note to geometric tilework.

name: Safran Strand
story: Saffron threads are prized for their golden color and aroma.

name: Kamoun Seed
story: Cumin seeds have a warm olive-brown surface.

name: Paprika Dust
story: Ground paprika gives spice markets a vivid red-orange note.

name: Zaatar Leaf
story: Dried thyme and zaatar blends range from sage to olive.

name: Ras El Hanout
story: The spice blend's ingredients create a layered rust-brown hue.

name: Sahara Dune
story: Dry dune sand shifts from pale gold to muted ochre.

name: Sahara Amber
story: Low desert light warms sand and stone toward amber.

name: Sahara Horizon
story: Open desert horizons often appear pale under strong daylight.

name: Sahara Shadow
story: Long shadows cool the earth tones of desert settlements.

name: Sahara Rose
story: Rose-colored mineral earth appears in parts of the southern landscape.

name: Marrakech Rouge
story: The Red City name reflects the warm earthen color of its walls.

name: Marrakech Terracotta
story: Terracotta tones echo the city's clay-colored architecture.

name: Chefchaouen Blue
story: Blue-painted walls are a prominent feature of Chefchaouen's medina.

name: Essaouira Blue
story: Blue boats and doors mark the Atlantic port's streetscape.

name: Majorelle Blue
story: The saturated blue is associated with the Majorelle Garden in Marrakech.

name: Medina Limewash
story: Limewashed surfaces soften light in historic medina streets.

name: Medina Door Green
story: Painted timber doors add green accents to many old-town facades.

name: Medina Ochre
story: Ochre plaster and stone create warm accents across old quarters.

name: Medina Indigo
story: Indigo-dyed textiles appear in markets and traditional clothing.

name: Medina Rose
story: Muted rose appears in plaster, textiles, and painted shutters.

name: Atay Mint
story: Fresh mint gives Moroccan tea its familiar aromatic garnish.

name: Atay Glass
story: Mint leaves steeped in tea lend a soft green association.

name: Atay Sugar
story: Sugar cones and cubes provide a pale cream counterpoint.

name: Atay Tea
story: Steeped green tea takes on an amber-brown tone.

name: Atay Tray
story: Aged serving trays range from warm brass to dark bronze.

name: Chouara Leather
story: The Chouara tannery in Fes is known for its traditional dye vats.

name: Tannery Poppy
story: Red dyes are among the recognizable colors produced in tanneries.

name: Tannery Saffron
story: Yellow dye vats lend a golden note to the tannery palette.

name: Tannery Indigo
story: Indigo dyes create deep blue shades in leather and cloth.

name: Tannery Olive
story: Olive leather tones sit between green dye and natural hide.

name: Zitoun Olive
story: Olive trees and cured olives are part of everyday Moroccan food culture.

name: Argan Leaf
story: Argan trees are native to a limited region of southwestern Morocco.

name: Henna Leaf
story: Henna leaves are dried and ground for traditional body art.

name: Rose of Dades
story: The Dades Valley is associated with rose cultivation and rose products.

name: Moroccan Fig Leaf
story: Fig trees are cultivated across several Moroccan growing regions.

name: Orange Blossom
story: Orange blossom water is used in Moroccan cooking and sweets.

name: Tadelakt Ivory
story: Tadelakt is a polished lime plaster traditionally associated with Marrakech.

name: Tadelakt Rose
story: Pigmented lime plaster can take on muted rose and terracotta tones.

name: Clay Red
story: Red clay is used in pottery and earthen construction.

name: Clay Sand
story: Sun-dried earthen materials range from tan to light brown.

name: Plaster Cream
story: Pale plaster reflects strong daylight across courtyard walls.

name: Textile Carmine
story: Carmine and madder reds are traditional textile dye colors.

name: Textile Indigo
story: Indigo is used to dye cloth in deep blue shades.

name: Atlas Wool
story: Undyed wool ranges from pale cream to warm natural brown.

name: Saffron Weave
story: Golden yarns add warmth to woven rugs and textiles.

name: Pomegranate Dye
story: Pomegranate rind has been used in traditional dyeing practices.
